# context-discipline: what it prints

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_demos.py from real runs; do not edit by
     hand. CI fails when this file no longer matches the code. -->

Real output of [context-discipline](../../plugins/context-discipline) on the fixtures its own
tests use. Skills and subagents are not shown: what they say depends on the
model, and they are measured by the eval cases in the plugin's `evals/`.

## check_claude_md.py on a CLAUDE.md whose rules get ignored

Each finding names the line and says what to write instead.

```console
$ python3 plugins/context-discipline/scripts/check_claude_md.py plugins/context-discipline/tests/fixtures/bad-CLAUDE.md
ERROR  line 16  [broken-import]
        imports missing-file.md, which does not exist
        → The import silently contributes nothing.
warn   line 3  [vague]
        'properly' promises a standard without naming one
        → Write what a reviewer could check: not "handle errors properly" but "never catch an exception without either re-raising it or logging it with the failing input".
warn   line 5  [vague]
        'best practice' promises a standard without naming one
        → Write what a reviewer could check: not "handle errors properly" but "never catch an exception without either re-raising it or logging it with the failing input".
warn   line 7  [emphasis]
        20 emphasis markers (ALWAYS, CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, MANDATORY, MUST)
        → Emphasis is a budget. Past about ten, none of it signals anything — spend it only on the handful of rules that must win over the rest.
warn   line 10  [no-alternative]
        prohibition with no alternative named
        → A rule that closes one door and opens none gets worked around. Say what to do instead, on the same line.
warn   line 14  [prose-block]
        1 very long paragraph(s)
        → Rules survive as short bullets. Prose reads as background and gets treated as background.

11 lines: 1 error(s), 5 warning(s), 0 note(s)
[exit 1]
```
